name: Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that the acceptable price band for our offering falls between [Price A] and [Price B]. We will verify this by surveying 50 qualified target customers using the four standard Van Westendorp questions, and consider it validated if the Indifference Price Point aligns with our planned market pricing within a ±10% margin.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Build the survey around the four price questions: too cheap, a bargain, getting expensive, too expensive.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Send the instrument only to qualified buyers who match the defined ideal customer profile.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Plot the cumulative curves; read the indifference and optimal price points and compare with the plan price.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Construct a survey detailing the core value proposition. Include the four standard pricing questions: (1) At what price is it too cheap to trust the quality? (2) A bargain? (3) Getting expensive, but still worth considering? (4) Too expensive to consider?

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Distribute the instrument strictly to qualified target buyers who match the defined ICP.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Plot cumulative distribution curves to identify the Indifference Price Point (intersection of "Cheap" and "Expensive") and the Optimal Price Point (intersection of "Too Cheap" and "Too Expensive"): Optimal Price Point (OPP) = Intersection of "Too Cheap" and "Too Expensive"

warning.label: Stated Willingness Bias
warning.text: Stated-price surveys overestimate what people pay when asked to enter real payment details.

warningFull: Theoretical pricing surveys reliably overestimate how much customers will actually spend when asked to enter real payment details.

origin.title: NSS-Price Sensitivity Meter (PSM): A New Approach to Study Consumer Perception of Price
